statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 13 of 100 in the low band, twelve points below the 25 block threshold, while stress falls to 72 in the high band and confidence is 89 on a fully verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The decisive evidence is the observed close, which resolved without one-way extension: NDX finished at 29,368.44, up 0.91% but 105 points below its 29,473.12 session high, and NQ near 29,380.25 is still capped by a 29,499.50 high that has held since midday. A market that closes more than a hundred points off its high after a broad advance is granting mean reversion rather than denying it, so neither the Friday weekly expiry nor the near-certain rate decision next Wednesday is treated as observed one-way structure. The named window covers 20:00 to 21:00 UTC, the thin post-close futures hour before the CME weekend halt, where conditional tail stays at 13 inside the low band. From 21:00 UTC the remaining twenty-three slots lie inside the weekend closure, and the 5 to 7 conditional floor published there is residual model uncertainty rather than a forecast of structure, because a persistent no-retracement path cannot form while the contract is not trading. Stress remains high at 72 and reflects an unresolved inflation impulse, crude above 100 dollars and a rate decision that is close to fully priced, none of which is a tail mechanism on its own.
headline: An orderly Friday close under an intact ceiling: NDX finished 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but 105 points below its 29,473.12 high, NQ near 29,380.25 remains capped by a 29,499.50 high that has held since midday, VIX closed 15.84 after an 11.2% collapse, and WTI eased to 100.25 as rate-hike odds for Wednesday jumped to roughly 87%.
body:
Both dated U.S. releases for Friday are verified and behind the market. The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC: all items rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over twelve months, while all items less food and energy rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above consensus, and 2.4% over the year. Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for more than a third of the monthly all-items increase, with energy up 2.1% on the month and 16.3% on the year. The University of Michigan preliminary September survey followed at 14:00 UTC at 47.8 against a 51.0 consensus and a 51.7 August final, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.6% and the longer-run measure at 3.4%.

The price path is now complete for the week and it granted mean reversion throughout. The cash session closed at 20:00 UTC with the Nasdaq-100 at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 daily range. The index finished 105 points below its own high, so the closing auction did not extend the advance. NQ futures trade near 29,380.25, up 0.84%, roughly 119 points under a 29,499.50 session high that has now capped the contract since midday, inside a 29,040.50 to 29,499.50 range. Breadth was broad rather than narrow, with all eleven S&P 500 sectors higher and every megacap positive, which supports direction but is not by itself evidence of a no-retracement path.

Cross-asset signals are mixed rather than aligned behind a single trend. Volatility collapsed: VIX closed at 15.84, down 11.2%, after trading from 17.71 down to 15.59. Crude eased, with WTI at 100.25 and 2.2% lower against a 102.48 prior close, although the weekly gain remains near 9% and Brent is close to 105 while the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed. Diesel at a record 6.05 dollars a gallon keeps the inflation impulse alive. Yields rose at the front end, with the two-year near 4.63% and the ten-year near 4.97%, as futures moved to roughly an 87% probability of a rate increase at Wednesday's decision, up from about 72% before the inflation print.

The forward horizon is dominated by structure rather than by risk. CME equity index futures halt at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until Sunday evening, beyond the end of this 24-hour window, so twenty-three of the twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market. Conditional tail is therefore published at a 5 to 7 residual floor across that stretch and the mode is normal, because the amplifiers that would justify a higher reading, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or price holding at session extremes, require an open tape. Stress decays to a weekend baseline near 32, a level held deliberately above zero to represent carried exposure into a week containing retail sales, the rate decision with projections, and an unconfirmed Gulf-Iran meeting on Hormuz reported for Monday.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 20:00 UTC on 10 September to 19:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 19 and 18 with the mode event/whipsaw across the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots around the previous cash close, then eases steadily through the overnight to a low of 11 as Asian and early European trade stayed orderly. The mode turns trend-up from 06:00 UTC through 11:00 UTC while the European session built a directional advance without denying retracement, with tail contained between 13 and 15. The only watch-band readings in the window are 21 and 22 in the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots, both marked event/whipsaw around the 12:30 UTC consumer price release, where confidence also fell to 70 and 80 while the outcome was still being absorbed. From 14:00 UTC the series returns to the low band and the mixed mode, holding 15 to 17 through the U.S. afternoon as price rotated beneath an unbroken high. Stress is the one genuinely elevated series across the whole window, starting at 87 and declining only gradually to 77 by the final slot, which is the signature of a difficult but recoverable environment rather than a lethal one.
outlookSummary: The forward window contains roughly twenty minutes of thin post-close futures trade and then spends its remaining twenty-three slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 13 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, covering the completed cash close and the thin hour that follows it. It drops to 7 as the halt takes effect, then settles on a 5 to 6 floor for every remaining hour. That floor is residual model uncertainty, not a forecast of structure, because a persistent no-retracement price path cannot form while the contract is not trading, and the dominant mode is published as normal for the entire closed stretch. Stress declines from 72 through 58 and 47 to a weekend baseline of 32, held above zero to represent carried exposure rather than a claim that the macro environment has calmed. Confidence decays gradually from 89 to 70 purely as a function of evidence age, since the newest verified observation is the 20:00 UTC Friday close and nothing inside the horizon can refresh it. The genuine checkpoints all sit beyond this window: the Sunday futures reopen, the unconfirmed Monday Gulf-Iran meeting on the Strait of Hormuz, and Wednesday's rate decision with projections.
